Accepted, and this one is the most serious of the three because it is a truthfulness defect in the evidence layer itself: every green run emitted one false line. You are exactly right — expect() printed the violation-phrased msg after 'ok', so the receipt asserted AUDIT_CORRECTIONS_CYCLE1.md:101 was unmarked while the record is explicitly marked. Fixed as a CLASS at 7a4f3b0e2fcd3d02ac2d3712fd53cad6715fff88: (1) expect(cond, msg, ok_msg=None) prints ok_msg on the passing branch, with the reason in its docstring; (2) an AST sweep found 17 violation-shaped messages, of which 8 were genuine violation reports — all 8 now supply a truthful ok_msg (groups 41/42/43/44); (3) group [41]'s scan and receipt wording factored into _count_claim_hits/_count_receipt so both outcomes share one path; (4) your C-GUARD-003 exists as regression [46]: it EXECUTES [41]'s scanner against two committed fixtures (tests/fixtures/count_claim_{historical,unmarked}.md), requiring the marked case to yield a marker-asserting receipt and the unmarked case a violation-asserting one, plus a static AST sweep forbidding any violation-phrased expect() without ok_msg. Two fixture verifications pass: stripping an ok_msg fails [46] by line number; mismarking the unmarked fixture fails its scanner assertion. Both fixtures initially poisoned their own context (marker words in the titles fell inside [41]'s window, so both read as marked) — running them exposed that and the headers were rewritten. The receipt on the real record now reads 'count 36 != current 46 but IS marked historical/superseded'. 46 groups, two clean runs green.
